metadata.difficulty_description: Moderate difficulty: 30-year-old man (less typical sex — NMDAR encephalitis is female-predominant but occurs in males). No teratoma. MRI has subtle bilateral temporal FLAIR changes that could be mistaken for HSV encephalitis. Antibodies pending — empirical HSV treatment initiated but encephalitis is autoimmune.

patient.presenting_complaint: Three-week history of progressive confusion, memory disturbance, and two witnessed convulsions
patient.hpi: A 30-year-old secondary school teacher was brought to the emergency department by his wife after a second witnessed generalised tonic-clonic seizure. His wife reported that over the preceding three weeks he had become increasingly forgetful and confused, losing track of conversations and on one occasion failing to recognise the route to his own school where he had taught for four years. He had also begun behaving oddly at home — making repetitive purposeless movements with his hands, and on several occasions repeating the same question within minutes without apparent awareness that he had just asked it. In the week before admission his personality had changed noticeably: he became irritable, suspicious, and at one point accused his wife of hiding things from him. His wife initially attributed these changes to work-related stress as he was preparing students for national exams. He had been seen by his GP approximately ten days before admission with complaints of poor sleep and low mood; the GP had prescribed a short course of zopiclone 7.5 mg at night and planned mental health follow-up. Two days before admission he had a brief (60-second) convulsive episode witnessed by his wife from which he recovered over about 20 minutes, and a second more prolonged (2-minute) seizure on the morning of admission prompted emergency services to be called. He had no past psychiatric history. He described a mild sore throat and low-grade fever approximately four weeks prior to onset that resolved without treatment. There is no family history of neurological or psychiatric disease. He does not smoke, drinks approximately 8 units alcohol per week, and uses no illicit substances. He takes no regular medications aside from the recently prescribed zopiclone.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis excluded based on sex — 'this is a female condition'
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis affects males and is not sex-exclusive. Approximately 35% of cases are male. In males, teratoma is less common but the clinical syndrome is identical.

red_herrings.data_point: Bilateral temporal MRI changes with low-grade fever
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: HSV encephalitis typically shows haemorrhagic temporal lesions with cortical ribboning on DWI, rapid progression, and higher CSF pleocytosis. The symmetric, non-haemorrhagic, DWI-negative bilateral temporal changes in this case are more consistent with autoimmune limbic encephalitis. HSV PCR negative confirms.

red_herrings.data_point: GP prescribed zopiclone for insomnia with apparent initial improvement
red_herrings.intended_effect: Stress-related insomnia and anxiety, not encephalitis
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Insomnia is an early prodromal feature of anti-NMDAR encephalitis — it represents hypothalamic dysfunction, not a psychiatric condition. Symptomatic improvement of insomnia with zopiclone does not address the underlying autoimmune process.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis — tumour-negative (idiopathic), male patient

differential.key_features: HSV PCR negative. MRI shows symmetric, non-haemorrhagic temporal changes (HSV typically haemorrhagic and asymmetric). Subacute 3-week course (HSV usually more acute). Anti-NMDAR antibodies confirmed.
LGI1 more common in older males with faciobrachial dystonic seizures. Anti-LGI1 antibodies negative.
All viral PCRs negative. Post-infectious NMDAR encephalitis possible after viral prodrome, but positive anti-NMDAR antibodies confirm autoimmune aetiology.
CT body and MRI show no mass lesion. No enhancement. Age and sex could overlap but CSF cytology negative.

optimal_actions.action: Urgent MRI brain with FLAIR and DWI to characterise temporal lobe involvement
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Bilateral temporal FLAIR hyperintensity — favours autoimmune limbic encephalitis over HSV (non-haemorrhagic, symmetric)

optimal_actions.action: EEG urgently — evaluate encephalopathic pattern and seizure risk
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Bilateral temporal rhythmic delta slowing — limbic encephalitis pattern

optimal_actions.action: Lumbar puncture with CSF analysis, viral PCR panel, and autoimmune encephalitis antibodies
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Moderate lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein, negative HSV PCR, anti-NMDAR antibodies pending

optimal_actions.action: Initiate empirical IV aciclovir pending HSV PCR — do not delay
optimal_actions.expected_finding: HSV must be empirically treated while awaiting PCR in any encephalitis with temporal lobe involvement

optimal_actions.action: Send anti-NMDAR antibodies (serum and CSF) and broader autoimmune encephalitis panel
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Positive anti-NMDAR CSF titre 1:80 — confirmed on day 5

optimal_actions.action: Stop aciclovir once HSV PCR negative and anti-NMDAR encephalitis confirmed. Initiate first-line immunotherapy.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: First-line: IVMP 1g/day × 5 days + IVIG 2 g/kg over 5 days

optimal_actions.action: CT body and testicular ultrasound to screen for paraneoplastic tumour
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No tumour identified in this case — idiopathic anti-NMDAR encephalitis

optimal_actions.action: Arrange 24-hour continuous EEG; start levetiracetam maintenance
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Subclinical seizures identified — levetiracetam dose escalation required

critical_actions: Do not dismiss anti-NMDAR encephalitis based on male sex — 35% of cases are male
Empirical aciclovir must be started pending HSV PCR given bilateral temporal changes
Stop aciclovir promptly when HSV PCR negative AND anti-NMDAR antibodies confirmed
Initiate immunotherapy (IVMP + IVIG) without further delay once anti-NMDAR encephalitis confirmed
Testicular ultrasound required for tumour screening in male patients
contraindicated_actions: Withhold empirical aciclovir in temporal encephalitis pending all test results
Continue aciclovir indefinitely after HSV PCR negative and autoimmune diagnosis confirmed
Delay immunotherapy awaiting complete antibody panel in a patient with deteriorating consciousness
Omit paraneoplastic tumour screening in male patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis
key_reasoning_points: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis occurs in males — failure to consider this diagnosis in a young man with subacute psychiatric and cognitive symptoms plus seizures is a common error.
Bilateral non-haemorrhagic temporal FLAIR changes differ from classical unilateral haemorrhagic HSV pattern — the agent must recognise this distinction to guide management.
Hyponatraemia from SIADH is a recognised complication of hypothalamic involvement in anti-NMDAR encephalitis, not an incidental finding.
In males without teratoma, anti-NMDAR encephalitis is 'idiopathic' — the absence of tumour does not change the immunotherapy approach but removes the benefit of tumour removal.
Subclinical electrographic seizures are common and missed without continuous EEG monitoring — levetiracetam is the anti-seizure drug of choice (non-enzyme-inducing).

findings.location: Medial temporal lobe (left hippocampus and amygdala)

mri.impression: Bilateral (left-predominant) medial temporal FLAIR signal abnormality. Urgent CSF with HSV PCR and autoimmune antibody panel required. Pattern differs from typical HSV in that it is symmetric and non-haemorrhagic. Clinical correlation recommended.

background.posterior_dominant_rhythm: Poorly organized theta activity, 6-7 Hz, replacing expected alpha rhythm

findings.morphology: Generalised diffuse slowing. Background frequency 5-6 Hz throughout. No posterior dominant rhythm. Disorganised pattern.
Intermittent rhythmic delta activity over bilateral temporal regions (left > right), frequency 1.5-2 Hz. Episodes last 10-20 seconds. Non-evolving.
No extreme delta brush. No generalised spike-and-wave complexes. No ictal activity captured. Pattern more consistent with encephalopathy than primary epilepsy.

eeg.impression: Moderate encephalopathic EEG. No extreme delta brush. No ictal activity. Clinical correlation recommended.

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: Sodium 129 mEq/L (L), Chloride 97 mEq/L (L), CRP 0.8 mg/dL (H), ESR 22 mm/hr (H), CK 148 U/L (H).

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 20 cmH2O. Protein: 0.61 g/L. Glucose: 3.4 mmol/L.

Anti-NMDA receptor IgG antibody is found in a subset of patients with autoimmune encephalitis; a positive result should be interpreted in the clinical context. Clinical correlation recommended.

results.title: Second-line immunotherapy in anti-NMDAR encephalitis: rituximab and cyclophosphamide
results.summary: For patients without a teratoma or those who do not respond to first-line therapy (IVMP + IVIG) within 2-4 weeks, second-line agents are recommended: Rituximab 375 mg/m² IV weekly × 4 doses (most commonly used; targets CD20+ B cells). Cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m² monthly for 3-6 months (alternative). Azathioprine or mycophenolate mofetil are used for long-term maintenance. With second-line therapy, an additional 30-40% of first-line non-responders achieve good outcomes.

findings.morphology: Persistently disorganised background. No extreme delta brush. Five subclinical electrographic seizures captured — bilateral temporal onset, brief (<45 seconds), no clinical correlate. Pattern consistent with anti-NMDAR encephalitis.

output.impression: Subclinical seizures on continuous EEG. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.query: Empirical aciclovir autoimmune encephalitis HSV negative when to stop

results.title: Management of empirical aciclovir in suspected encephalitis
results.summary: UK/international guidelines recommend empirical IV aciclovir (10 mg/kg 8-hourly) in all suspected encephalitis pending HSV PCR result. HSV PCR sensitivity is >95% in the appropriate temporal window. When CSF HSV PCR is negative AND MRI pattern does not suggest HSV AND clinical course >7-10 days, aciclovir can be safely discontinued. Symmetric non-haemorrhagic temporal involvement and absence of cortical ribboning on DWI favours autoimmune over viral aetiology. Confirm anti-NMDAR antibodies before definitively stopping aciclovir.
